newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says Australian outlook is very good.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says Australian outlook is very good.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, commenting on the latest monetary policy easing by the Reserve Bank, said on Wednesday that the nation now had a very good outlook for the coming year.

The central bank, which cut the official cash rate by 50 basis points to 5.0 percent earlier in the day, has now eased monetary policy five times in the last 12 months, citing low inflation and the need to get the economy moving and unemployment lower.

Costello referred to a raft of good economic news released in the past week, including record low inflation, a better-than-expected budget outcome, a record monthly trade surplus and Wednesday's fifth rate cut.
"This is a conjunction of very significant economic news which sets Australia up for a very good outlook over the forthcoming year," he said.
He said the rate cuts announced in late 1996 were still working their way through the economy and that the benefits of the remaining two rate cuts were yet to materialise.

The central bank began lowering rates last July, with two cuts in the final few months of 1996, one on May 23 this year, and again on Wednesday. Each time it reduced the official cash rate by 50 basis points.
"Interest rates work their way through the economy on a 12 month to 18 month delay," Costello said.
"What that means is that we are now - business is now -- just starting to feel the benefits of rate reductions that were occurring in the latter part of last year," he said.
